subject: Re: ROAR benchmark kickoff — scoring interpretability methods
body: Status ahead of the sweep week. Pipeline repro is done: base ResNet-50s train to 76.0% top-1 on ImageNet in our setup, and the ROAR mechanics (rank inputs per estimator, remove the top fraction, retrain from scratch) are validated end-to-end on the 10%-removal slice. Early signal matches the paper's headline: gradient-based saliency barely beats a random-removal baseline once you retrain, while the ensemble variants degrade accuracy much faster — exactly the separation ROAR exists to expose. Ops notes: Leilani's launcher packs 16-GPU slices well (dry run hit 88% utilization), and checkpoint/removal artifacts land in Corpus without issues. Risk: estimator #5 (the SmoothGrad variant) is 3× slower at ranking than budgeted; Gustavo is precomputing its rankings this week so ranking never blocks a training slot during the June window. — Efe
